newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario lawyers' groups suing accountants.
newsitem.headline: Ontario lawyers' groups suing accountants.

text.p: The Law Society of Upper Canada and the Lawyers' Professional Indemnity Company (LPIC) said on Friday that they started legal action against their former auditors, Ernst & Young, and their former actuaries, Tillinghast, a Towers Perrin Company.
The two Ontario lawyers' organizations said they sought damages of C$110 million for alleged breach of contract, negligence and negligent misstatement, together with remedial and investigative costs.
Ernst and Young spokesman Dave Rowney told Reuters that the company believed the complaint was without merit.
"Ernst and Young has received a copy of a complaint which has been recently filed by the Law Society of Upper Canada, he said in Ernst's official statement.

"After a review of the complaint it is our view that the claim against us is without merit. We are satisfied that our work was performed with due care and in accordance with professional standards and we will vigorously defend our position."
A spokesman for Tillinghast told Reuters the company could not comment on the lawsuit for fear of prejudicing the case.

In their statement of claim, the lawyers' organizations alleged inaccurate financial information was provided by Ernst & Young and Tillinghast concerning the deficits in the lawyers' insurance program and in the level of claim liabilities.
The claim further alleged that due to audit and actuarial errors, the deficit was seriously understated from 1990 to 1993.
The Law Society is the governing body of the Ontario legal profession. The LPIC provides liability insurance to more than 16,000 lawyers in Ontario.
